Wood in lower Lake Marion off Rowland and White Oak from the 11/2 recordings: where the CHIRP stood 2 ft or more off a flat bottom, Claude read the ClearVu picture (answers.json) and I read it beside it (review_1102.json). Agreed pieces carry the top; the ones we differ on, or neither of us can tell, are "unsure" with no top. Fish we both called fish are left out.

level.source: USGS 02169921 00062, the NGVD29 series (the app reads the same gauge for Lake Marion; full pool 76.8 ft NGVD29)
level.note: level_ft is the gauge at the 15-minute reading nearest the read; below_full_pool_ft = 76.8 - level_ft. Today's top = top_ft - (feet below full pool today - below_full_pool_ft): a lake lower today brings the top nearer the surface.

_fields.kind: wood (stands 2 ft or more off the bottom), low_wood (under 2 ft), no_height (seen only off to the side by the side-imaging finder; never gone over), unsure (Claude's read and the desktop's differ, or neither could tell; no top)
_fields.reads[].top_ft / bottom_ft: feet below the surface on the sounder at the time of the read (ClearVu, the kayak over it)
_fields.reads[].read_by: claude_api = Claude through the Worker's /claude/look; desktop = the desktop Claude session reading the same picture
_fields.reads[].confirmed_by_ryan: true where Ryan answered for that day's pictures (10/31: 'the ones that look like stumps and trees are stumps and trees')
_fields.reads[].level_ft / below_full_pool_ft: the lake gauge at the read, where the app has one for this water; null where it has none
_fields.lat / lon: the kayak's GPS fix when it was over the top (WGS84)
